rubriker.title: Critical thinking takes centre stage at Judit Polgar's Global Chess Festival
rubriker._rss_content: The 12th Judit Polgar Global Chess Festival took place at the Hungarian National Gallery in Budapest, with critical thinking as the central theme of its 2026 edition. The programme combined chess with education, technology and art, and included a Community Chess Simul with the strongest female chess player of all time, the public debut of the RubikChess Tournament, AI-related activities and a range of events aimed at families and young players. | Photo: Global Chess Festival

rubriker.title: El Global Chess Festival, organizado por Judit Polgar, vuelve a conquistar Budapest
rubriker._rss_content: La 12.ª edición del «Global Chess Festival», liderado por Judit Polgar, se celebró en la Galería Nacional de Hungría, en Budapest. El pensamiento crítico fue el tema central de la edición de 2026. El programa combinó el ajedrez con la educación, la tecnología y el arte, e incluyó una exhibición de simultáneas comunitarias con la mejor ajedrecista de todos los tiempos, el debut público del torneo RubikChess, actividades relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial y una serie de propuestas dirigidas a familias y jóvenes ajedrecistas. | Foto: Global Chess Festival

rubriker.title: From Tsaghkadzor to the Grand Final: European Schools Chess Champions crowned amidst cultural celebration
rubriker._rss_content: Gymnasium No. 50 of Minsk won the European Continental Stage of the FIDE ISCF World Schools Team Championship in Tsaghkadzor, completing the eight-round event with a perfect match score. Riga State Gymnasium No. 1 took second place, while LEPL Georgia, Kutaisi Andria Razmadze Physico finished third. The champions also secured qualification for December's Grand Final, with individual board prizes and a closing ceremony bringing the European stage to an end. | Photos: Arlan Olzhabay / BI-Group
